newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

Vice-President of the Samsung Corporation Pil-Gon Rhee said many loose agreements existed in East Asia for private firms to undertake infrastructure projects but in reality very few were actually acted upon. Rhee spoke at a conference on public and private investment in infrastructure in East Asia.
Indonesia will not change its national car policy and will not back down if Japan takes the matter to the World Trade Organization (WTO) said Minister for Trade and Industry Tungky Ariwibowo.

Minister of Science and Technology Jusuf Habibie on a visit to Malaysia proposed to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad that the two countries could cooperate in the production of Indonesia's N-250 aircraft. He said that Malaysia could make spare parts for Indonesian aircraft manufacturer IPTN.
Coordinating Minister for Security and Politics Susilo Sudarman has repeated warnings that the foreign press is unreliable and sometimes even lies.
